## Exercise: decide whether a network has an Eulerian trail

Two problems, both ending in the same question Euler asked. Expect about an hour.

1. **Binghamton, not Königsberg.** Turn the rivers and bridges of Binghamton, NY into a graph of landmasses and bridges, build its adjacency matrix, and decide whether you can cross every bridge exactly once.
2. **A network you did not draw.** Pick any network under 5,000 nodes from [Netzschleuder](https://networks.skewed.de/), load its edge list with `pandas`, build the adjacency matrix from it, draw it, and run the same test.

The second one is the point of the exercise: your Euler test has to work on data you have never looked at, which means it has to be written in terms of degrees rather than in terms of a picture.

**[Open the exercise notebook]({{< var molab.m01_exercises >}})** — it runs in your
browser, with nothing to install and nothing to sign into.

Prefer to work locally? The notebook is in the repository at
[`notebooks/m01-euler-tour/03-exercises.py`](https://github.com/skojaku/adv-net-sci/blob/main/notebooks/m01-euler-tour/03-exercises.py).
Run it with `marimo edit notebooks/m01-euler-tour/03-exercises.py`.
